issue_context.title: Report a possible race that uses goroutines on shared variables.
issue_context.body:
**What did you see instead? Under which circumstances?**

At https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/main/tsdb/db_test.go#L708
https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/a7d499e19a932f4f7cf14e8b8c935dd43d2a9830/tsdb/db_test.go#L708

Within a loop "for _, c := range cases {", variable `db` is shared by all the loop iterations since it is defined outside the loop:

```
db := openTestDB(t, nil, nil)
for _, c := range cases {
		db, err = Open(snap, nil, nil, nil, nil)
		defer func() { require.NoError(t, db.Close()) }()
}
```

All the defer statements within the loop may refer to the last value updated by the loop. As a consequence, the last `db` may be closed multiple times, while the other `db`s are not closed.

More information on the bug can be found at https://github.com/golang/go/wiki/CommonMistakes#using-goroutines-on-loop-iterator-variables.

**What did you expect to see?**

A fix is to add `db` as a parameter to the closure so that `db` is evaluated at each iteration and placed on the stack for the goroutine rather than being shared.
```
db := openTestDB(t, nil, nil)
for _, c := range cases {
		db, err = Open(snap, nil, nil, nil, nil)
		defer func(db *DB) { require.NoError(t, db.Close()) }(db)
}
```
Another fix is to introduce a local storage for `db`:
```
db := openTestDB(t, nil, nil)
for _, c := range cases {
		db, err := Open(snap, nil, nil, nil, nil)
		defer func() { require.NoError(t, db.Close()) }()
}
```

Found by #deepgo.
comments: Thanks for the report. We should not override the `db` since it is used for delete at the start of the loop, and we cannot do a `:=` later in the loop with `db`, so a suggested way is to rename the `db` in the loop to something like `newDB`. Additionally, we should have a `db.Close()` for the one opened outside the loop.

review_comments: We should now have `defer func() { require.NoError(t, db.Close()) }()` for the db created at line 665, right after it is created.
should we use Subtests to call this inner defer more often?
We can skip the subtest in this PR. To enable having >1 case (currently we have only 1 case) we require some refactoring anyway, so could be done with that (if we ever get to it).
